case_title: Deepak @ Wireless v. State of Maharashtra
evidence_type: Eyewitness (injured victim PW9); oral evidence of PW2 on stolen property; medical (PW1 postmortem doctor); recovery/seizure (PW4 panch witness, spot panchnama Ext. 28); test of identification in court
aggravating_circumstances: Murder of the victim's brother-in-law by group of five using knives and rods; grievous injuries to PW9, who was also assaulted after witnessing the attack
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.395, 396 and 397 IPC; RI 5 years and Rs.500 fine (s.395, default 3 years RI); life RI and Rs.500 fine (s.396); RI 3 years and Rs.500 fine (s.397, default 1 year RI)
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence confirmed
offence_finally_established: Dacoity with murder and grievous hurt (robbery) under IPC ss.395, 396 and 397
neutral_facts: In the early hours of 14 June 2004, at about 2 to 2.30 a.m., a group of men entered the house of the victims. The victim's brother-in-law was beaten with knives, an iron rod and a wooden club and died from his injuries. When the victim, the brother-in-law's sister-in-law, began shouting, the assailants turned on her and struck her on the eyes, head and back. She was left seriously injured and could not speak when brought to hospital. She told police that four to five men were involved, wearing pants and shirts, and that they fled on a motorcycle. At trial, in cross-examination, she stated that the number of persons was five. She identified the accused in court and described the clothing and physical features of the attackers. Police had earlier stopped a motorcycle carrying three fleeing men; two were apprehended, one of them the accused, and a third escaped. At the time of arrest, a knife, a motorcycle key and cash were seized from the accused, and the seizure was witnessed by a panch witness. The accused's clothes were examined and found to have blood stains. The victim's husband stated that cash of about Rs.4,000 to 5,000 and the ornaments worn by the victim were taken, and a spot panchnama recorded in his presence noted disturbed household articles and a forced window. A post-mortem doctor gave evidence on the head injuries and cause of death and on the injuries to the victim. The motorcycle used by the group had been stolen earlier and was recovered. Two of the men were juveniles and were dealt with separately, and two others remained absconding. Charge sheet was filed against the accused and the others.
physical_harm: Death of the victim's brother-in-law (cardio-respiratory arrest due to head injury, with asphyxia from blood aspiration; 11 injuries). Victim PW9 suffered incised wounds to forehead, eye and cheek, contusion, and fracture of mandible; hospitalised for 2-3 months with disabled movements.
financial_property_loss: Cash of approximately Rs.4,000 to 5,000 and ornaments worn by the victim
motive: Theft/robbery of cash and ornaments (court accepted an act of theft by the accused and others)
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of PW9 (injured eyewitness) on number of assailants (five) and her in-court identification of the appellant; PW2's evidence on stolen cash and ornaments, accepted with spot panchnama Ext. 28; PW1 postmortem and injury evidence; PW4 panch witness on seizure of clothes, knife, motorcycle key and cash
witness_credibility: PW9 found credible: first-hand witness who suffered injuries, definite answer in cross-examination on five assailants, unhesitant identification; slip in chief examination about stolen articles excused because of her serious injuries. PW2 evidence unshaken in cross-examination.
post_offence_conduct: Fled on a motorcycle at high speed, abandoned it and ran into an open field when chased; two men apprehended by police, the appellant among them
trial_duration: offence: 13/14.06.2004; trial judgment: 09.05.2005; High Court: 25.04.2007; Supreme Court: 04.09.2012
legal_representation: Accused/appellant: Rajiv Nanda. State/respondent: Aprajita Sinha and Asha Gopalan Nair
investigation_status: Investigation completed; charge sheet filed; trial completed with 10 prosecution witnesses
procedural_irregularity: No test identification parade held (raised by defence; court held it not fatal on these facts); wooden articles not seized in panch's presence; no comparison of blood group with the deceased (raised by defence)
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.395, 396, 397 with life and fixed sentences. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence confirmed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: PW9 was an eyewitness who identified the appellant without hesitation; her cross-examination fixes five participants; PW2 specified stolen cash and jewellery; non-recovery explained by the absconding accused; PW8's recovered motorcycle supports the case; relied on Rafiq Ahmad
defence_argument: Five-person requirement not proved; no recovery of looted articles or weapons; blood on clothes not compared with the deceased's group; no test identification parade; PW9 never deposed to theft of jewels; false case by police
legal_principle_applied: Under ss.395-397 IPC, participation with five or more persons in robbery that results in murder and attempted death or grievous hurt with deadly weapons is sufficient; knife is a deadly weapon; a credible victim-witness's unhesitant identification can be relied upon without test identification parade where circumstances allow
precedent_relied_upon: Relied on: Dana Yadav alias Dadu v. State of Bihar (2002) 7 SCC 295; Simon and others v. State of Karnataka (2004) 2 SCC 694; Daya Singh v. State of Haryana AIR 2001 SC 1188. Distinguished: Mohd. Abdul Hafeez v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1983) 1 SCC 143. Referred to: Suraj Pal v. State of Haryana (1995) 2 SCC 64. Cited: Rafiq Ahmad v. State of Uttar Pradesh (2011) 8 SCC 300.
judicial_aggravating_factors: Involvement of a group of five, murder of the deceased, and grievous injuries to PW9
